text:
incident-bot: PAGER — High token usage detected for tenant VELA (dedicated pool: vela-prod). Severity: P1. Alert: sudden spike in per-request token counts starting ~2026-03-14T18:02Z. Potential billing impact and quota exhaustion. Runbook: /runbooks/token-usage. Please ack and triage.

Sophia: acked, I'm on it. pulling recent logs and token histograms. pinging vela-sre.

Carmen: seeing a 20x jump in median tokens for VELA at ~18:02 UTC. avg 150 -> 3200 for text-generation calls. Same model variant (gptx-8k).

Eli: any deploys around that time?

Carmen: none in our infra. client-side deploy recorded by VELA at 18:01 (per webhook).

Raj: taking ownership from Sophia for on-call handoff. Sophia, drop any notes you have. I'll coordinate infra & billing.

Sophia: notes: sample request payloads attached in logs show large sequences of \"weird\" characters, and tokenizer breakdown shows long tokenized sequences (many small tokens). suspect encoding/misaligned tokenizer. here's a sample (redacted):

```
{
  "input": "\uFEFF\u0000H\u0000i\u0000 \u0000\ud83d\ude00 ...",
  "model": "gptx-8k",
  "tenant_id": "vela",
  "client_version": "vela-sdk/2.1.4"
}
```

Sophia: raw bytes look like UTF-16LE with BOM; our edge expects UTF-8 normalised strings. If client sent UTF-16, our tokenizer (which assumes UTF-8) is tokenizing differently -> massively inflated token counts.

vela-sre: confirming we shipped a client patch at 18:01 that toggled internal string encoding for some endpoints. We're investigating.

Eli: ok this explains why only VELA is affected (their client change) and why tokens blow up. Immediate mitigations: 1) apply per-tenant soft token cap + automatic truncation; 2) enable input normalization on the edge for vela-prod (convert UTF-16->UTF-8); 3) route VELA traffic to a smaller-context variant for short term to limit cost.

Raj: I'm going to apply a per-tenant rate-limit and token cap on the dedicated pool now. Carmen/ops-oncall: can you prepare the edge patch for normalization as a hotfix? we need a quick rollback mitigation if it affects valid customers.

ops-oncall: prepping an nginx-level transform that will detect BOM/UTF-16 patterns and normalize to UTF-8, will test on staging then promote to vela-prod canary. ETA 12m.

Carmen: applied tenant-level token cap (max_tokens_per_request=2000) and temporary truncate policy for VELA. Observing immediate reduction in token bill out. (rule id: tenant:vela:temp-cap-176543).

billing: flagged billing alerts for VELA, created provisional bill correction ticket and paused auto-billing for the spike window. We'll coordinate credits once root cause confirmed.

support: contacting VELA account team and SRE to notify them of mitigation steps and request rollback of client-side change if possible. Keeping customer in loop.

vela-sre: we're rolling back the client patch now and will push a corrected client (2.1.5) that emits UTF-8 by default. thanks for the quick mitigation.

Eli: monitoring token counts and request latencies. token histograms trending down after cap/normalization canary. still seeing some outliers from older clients.

Sophia: running tokenizer regression tests against a corpus with mixed encodings to validate edge normalization. early results look good.

Raj: handoff note: if normalization can be applied safely, promote to all vela-prod edge nodes. If we see any regressions, revert normalization and rely on cap + customer rollback.

ops-oncall: canary pushed to 10% of vela-prod traffic at 18:15Z. Token tail reduced from 3500->400 where canary applied. increasing to 50% now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — Mitigations applied (tenant cap, canary normalization, client rollback initiated). Severity downgraded to P2. Continue monitoring for billing impact.

billing: starting manual reconciliation for the spike window 18:01-18:20Z. We'll propose a customer credit and waive auto-billing for that window. Ticket: BILL-5942.

support: VELA acknowledged and confirmed rollback of their SDK to 2.1.3 internally. They requested a postmortem and the specific token metric samples.

Eli: root-cause summary (preliminary): VELA SDK 2.1.4 started sending UTF-16LE payloads with BOM for some text pipelines. Our tokenizer expects UTF-8; the encoding mismatch caused many code units to be interpreted as extra bytes producing inflated tokenization. Not an inferencing bug, but input encoding mismatch leading to billing/limits impact.

Sophia: next steps/ACs: 
- infra: ship edge normalization to all vela-prod nodes (ops)
- runtime: add a defensive pre-processor that normalizes input encoding and warns when non-UTF8 is detected (Eli/Carmen)
- billing: propose credit for VELA for spike window and prevent automated overages (billing)
- devex: add a note in client SDK guideline docs about encoding (support)
- postmortem: full RCA + timeline and customer comms (owner: Raj)

Raj: assigning postmortem owner: Raj. ETA draft in 48h. Will include code snippets, telemetry, and suggested SDK checks.

vela-sre: thanks for the rapid response — client patch rollback confirmed and we're testing 2.1.5. Please share reconciliation results.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — Primary mitigations in place, service normalized for vela-prod. Closing the pager but keeping thread open for postmortem and billing follow-up.

Sophia: marking action items in the incident board: INC-vela-176543. I'll attach tokenizer test vectors.

billing: created credit proposal: credit = estimated overage cost for spike window + 10% goodwill. sending to finance for approval.

Raj: final note — we should consider adding an edge heuristic that detects likely non-UTF8/UTF-16 payloads and returns a 400 with a helpful message (or auto-normalize with a header opt-in). We'll discuss in postmortem.

support: looping in customer-success to coordinate formal comms to VELA.

Carmen: closing monitoring loop. no further token anomalies for vela in the last 2h.

vela-sre: closing on our side too. thanks.

-- end of thread --
